observation: Two detection-only rounds bracket the useful Hough range for this scan. Round 1 (binary 110, oblique 35/65, horizontal 40/15, tolerance 12) lifted proxy 0.5435 -> 0.5774 and correspondence_f1@15 0.213 -> 0.275. Round 2 pushed further (binary 100, oblique 30/75, tolerance 15) and regressed slightly to 0.5740 / f1 0.269: the refreshed detected_lines.png shows the extra oblique segments landing on bolt-hole rows (more orange 'unexplained' joint lines in sc_correspondence_overlay.png) rather than new joints, so precision fell faster than recall rose. Stages 1-3 are unchanged and healthy across all rounds (recentre residual 2 cm, orient_axis_corr 0.967, depth_nan_ratio 20.9% family-normal, ring_count_error 0, 10 verticals at ~360 px = 1800 mm segment width at 5 mm/px). sam_fill_rate is bit-identical (0.7318) in anchor, R1 and R2, so SAM coverage is not the lever; the only movable lean feature is line/boundary agreement. Crucially, initial_prompt_points.png still shows 4/10 'assume' centres (x~180, 2520, 2880, 3240; det_real_detection_ratio 0.6) in both rounds even though bracketing oblique pairs now exist on those rings: ring x~2520-2880 has a red line at y~1450-1510 and a green line at y~1720-1780 (spacing ~210-330 px depending on x because the slopes are opposite), and ring x~2160-2520 has a pair at y~3400-3470 / 3730-3790 (~300 px). The K_height prior is 1226.97 mm = 245 px, so these pairs miss the distance-pattern check by ~20-60 px; tolerance 15 was not enough to convert any of them (the one accepted 'midpoint' at x~1620 had a ~255 px pair). sam_segment_size_cv 1.09 remains consistent with assumed centres landing off the true block rows.
rule: Ontology d8 (m_spacing_regularity poor vs K/AB pattern) -> stage_4_detection.f_pattern_mismatch, inter-stage chain f_pattern_mismatch -> stage_5_segmentation.f_crop_offset; remediation r_fix_height_priors (p_pattern_tolerance, pixel priors unchanged since resolution is unchanged). d7/f_missing_lines is now largely addressed at the round-1 Hough setting; r_relax_hough beyond it triggered the d9/f_spurious_lines side (bolt-row lines), so the Hough gates are returned to the round-1 optimum rather than relaxed further. Experiences section 5: more lines is not better, consistency with the ring/block pattern is; section 7/section 4: SAM geometry (segment_width/K_height/angle) stays at tunnel priors because det_real_detection_ratio has not risen and geometry knobs are load-bearing for transfer; section 3: do not chase the family-normal NaN fraction with denoising/enhancing changes.
failure_mode: stage_4_detection.f_pattern_mismatch (bracketing oblique pairs on the four fallback rings are rejected by check_distance_pattern at tolerance 12-15 px against the 245 px K prior and the rings drop to 'assume'), with residual f_spurious_lines from the round-2 over-relaxation, propagating to stage_5 f_crop_offset.
rationale: Single-lever final round. Restore the Hough/binarisation gates to the round-1 optimum (binary_threshold 110, hough_threshold_oblique 35, maxLineGap_oblique 65, horizontal 40/15) because round 2 showed the extra relaxation only added bolt-row lines and cost proxy; then push the one lever not yet exhausted, pattern_tolerance, to its bound 12 -> 20 so the ~250-300 px K-bracketing intersections on the currently assumed rings are accepted as real (midpoint) centres instead of falling back. Relative to round 1 the only change is pattern_tolerance, so the delta is cleanly attributable; false-match risk from the wider tolerance is bounded because the tighter round-1 Hough gates keep the line set small (minLineLength fixed), merge_close_points still collapses near-duplicates, and the ring count/verticals are already exact. hough_threshold_vertical untouched (ring_count_error 0). Denoising, enhancing and SAM template geometry left at priors: sam_fill_rate has been invariant across rounds, NaN is family-normal, and det_real_detection_ratio has not yet risen, which the round-2 plan set as the precondition for touching SAM geometry. Expected signal: det_real_detection_ratio 0.6 -> >=0.7, correspondence_f1@15 >= round-1 0.275, sam_segment_size_cv falling below ~1.0; if instead f1 returns to ~0.275 with 'assume' count unchanged, round 1 remains the selected round.
